result.target_topic: Remaining performance obligations and revenue recognition timeline
result.target_summary: Revenue allocated to remaining performance obligations was $1.1 billion as of January 28, 2024, consisting of contracted license, development, and hardware/software support arrangements. The company expects to recognize approximately 40% of this revenue over the next twelve months, with the remainder thereafter, excluding contracts with a length of one year or less.

target_year_over_year_context.explanation: Both disclosures report the total value of revenue allocated to remaining performance obligations and the expected timing of recognition. D093 cites $652 million with ~47% recognized over 12 months (P118_S003), while D106 cites $1.1 billion with ~40% recognized over 12 months (P117_S003, P117_S004). They describe the same specific financial metric.

previous_disclosures.summary: As of January 29, 2023, $652 million of revenue related to performance obligations had not been recognized, with approximately 47% expected to be recognized over the next twelve months, excluding contracts of one year or less.

current_disclosures.summary: Revenue allocated to remaining performance obligations was $1.1 billion as of January 28, 2024, consisting of contracted license, development, and hardware/software support arrangements. The company expects to recognize approximately 40% of this revenue over the next twelve months, with the remainder thereafter, excluding contracts with a length of one year or less.

materiality_analysis.reason: The disclosure of remaining performance obligations increased significantly from $652 million in 2023 to $1.1 billion in 2024 (a ~70% increase). This represents a substantial growth in deferred/receivable revenue, indicating a significant expansion in the company's backlog and future revenue visibility. The change in magnitude is material to financial condition and operational expectations.
materiality_analysis.key_change: Significant increase in remaining performance obligations

current_disclosures.summary: As of January 26, 2025, revenue related to remaining performance obligations from contracts greater than one year in length was $1.7 billion, comprising $1.6 billion from deferred revenue and $151 million unbilled and unrecognized. Approximately 39% of this revenue is expected to be recognized over the next twelve months.

materiality_analysis.reason: Revenue allocated to remaining performance obligations increased from $1.1 billion to $1.7 billion, a 54% increase. This signifies a material growth in NVIDIA's backlog of long-term contracted obligations, providing visibility into future revenue streams and reflecting strong customer commitment.
materiality_analysis.key_change: Substantial growth in remaining performance obligations

comparisons.peer_topic: Remaining Performance Obligations Balance and Recognition
comparisons.peer_summary: As of December 28, 2024, the aggregate transaction price allocated to remaining performance obligations under contracts with an original expected duration of more than one year was $85 million, of which $67 million is expected to be recognized in the next 12 months.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVDA and AMD disclose the aggregate transaction price allocated to remaining performance obligations under contracts with an original expected duration of more than one year. NVDA reports a significantly larger balance of $1.1 billion as of January 28, 2024, with approximately 40% expected to be recognized over the next twelve months. In contrast, AMD reports a much smaller balance of $85 million as of December 28, 2024, with $67 million expected to be recognized in the next 12 months. Both companies explicitly exclude contracts with an original expected duration of one year or less from these figures.

sentences.text: Revenue allocated to remaining performance obligations, which includes deferred revenue and amounts that will be invoiced and recognized as revenue in future periods, was $1.1 billion as of January 28, 2024.
We expect to recognize approximately 40% of this revenue over the next twelve months and the remainder thereafter.
This excludes revenue related to performance obligations for contracts with a length of one year or less.

As of December 28, 2024, the aggregate transaction price allocated to remaining performance obligations under contracts with an original expected duration of more than one year was $85 million, of which $67 million is expected to be recognized in the next 12 months.
The revenue allocated to remaining performance obligations does not include amounts which have an original expected duration of one year or less.
